The reported contrasts index social exclusion versus inclusion (an emotion induction) but do not constitute an instructed regulation contrast or a passive unregulated viewing contrast of emotional pictures as defined by the inclusion criteria, so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from E1–E5 are clearly met based on the record.

While this is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with instructed voluntary emotion regulation (attentional deployment; I2), reports within-group contrasts (I5) and has an eligible sample (I4), the NeuroStore record indicates the regulated emotional stimuli are primarily auditory (aversive sounds) and monetary outcomes rather than visual emotional stimuli, so the visual-stimuli requirement is not met (I3 not met). Additionally, the shared record explicitly lists 'Spatial scope: region of interest' and an 'FWE small-volume correction' inference, indicating results are reported as ROI/SVC rather than whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps (I6 not met). Therefore the study fails I3 and I6 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI/SVC results reported).

Met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample acceptable), I6 (whole-brain coordinates reported), I7 (reporting acceptable). Not met: I2 (no evidence the task instructed an emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal) and I5 (no within-group emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported; the listed analysis is an omnibus between-group contrast). The record shows only a between-group omnibus contrast, so exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task effect).

Based on the NeuroStore record, this is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with an eligible sample (I4) and it reports whole-brain group analyses with coordinates in MNI (I6). However, the task is autobiographical memory retrieval using personalized cues (textual cues), and the record does not indicate an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I2 not met). The stimuli appear to be personalized cues (text/sentences) rather than visual emotional images or films (I3 not met). The reported contrasts are memory retrieval versus ISI or condition comparisons (EAM, SAM) and do not isolate an emotion regulation attempt or a passive viewing of emotional visual stimuli as required (I5 not met). No full-text exclusion criteria from E1–E5 are indicated by the record.

I1 and I4 are met (task-based fMRI; sample acceptable). Excluded because multiple required inclusion criteria are not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation instruction — participants were told to imagine scenes without regulation instructions), I3 (stimuli are script-driven auditory narratives, not visual stimuli), I5 (reported contrasts are between-group interaction, not within-group regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), and I6 (results are multivariate whole-brain connectivity/network analyses rather than group-level, univariate voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates). Exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (only between-group contrasts / interaction reported, no within-group task effect) therefore apply.

The NeuroStore record describes a face-processing task with implicit emotion processing (identify oval colour; do not label facial expressions) and reports group-level whole-brain and ROI activation and PPI connectivity results. However, the record does not indicate any instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, increase, decrease instructions), so inclusion criterion I2 (task includes an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. Additionally, the extracted analyses are labeled as between-group or omnibus effects (no within-group task-effect contrasts for any group are reported in the NeuroStore record), which meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect). Other inclusion criteria appear met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample acceptable), I5 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: emotional faces > shapes), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis with reported peaks), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported). Because I2 is required and E4 applies, the study is excluded.

This article is a coordinate-based meta-analysis (MKDA) of published fMRI studies rather than an original task-based fMRI experiment, so it meets exclusion criterion E1. The NeuroStore record indicates tasks involved passive viewing (no instructed regulation), so I2 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy) is not met. The record does show visual stimuli (I3), healthy participants (I4), within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (I5), and whole-brain MKDA peaks in MNI space (I6). I1 (this article being a task-based fMRI study with original data) is not met. Therefore excluded under E1.

The NeuroStore record indicates this study reports structural MRI analyses (diffusion metrics and gray/white matter morphometry) rather than task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation to visual stimuli. Therefore it fails full-text inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (visual emotional stimuli), and I5 (within-task emotion regulation or passive viewing contrasts). It does meet I4 (acceptable sample) and I6 (group-level whole-brain results with coordinates reported).

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state fMRI study (Rest Task, eyes closed) reporting intrinsic functional connectivity (iFC) and fALFF pre-post changes following CBT versus control. This is not a task-based emotion regulation study with visual stimuli. Thus it fails multiple required inclusion criteria: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met; I2 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) not met; I3 (visual emotional stimuli) not met; I5 (within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation) not met; I6 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) not met. Inclusion criterion I4 (sample eligibility) is met. Full-text exclusion criteria E3 (resting-state or intrinsic connectivity only, no task activation map) applies. E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect) also applies because the reported effects are group x time differences in resting connectivity rather than within-task regulation contrasts.

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state, seed-based connectivity study rather than a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment. It therefore fails multiple required inclusion criteria: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state), I5 (no within-task emotion-regulation or passive viewing contrasts), and I6 (no task-evoked group-level whole-brain activation map). The only inclusion criterion clearly met from the record is I4 (sample description acceptable). Full-text exclusion criterion E3 applies because the paper reports only seed-based resting-state connectivity results with no accompanying whole-brain task activation map. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI face-processing study (I1) using visual face stimuli (I3) in a healthy child sample (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts reflecting unregulated viewing of emotional faces (e.g. Neutral, Sad, Fear) (I5) and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates (I6, I7). The record does not indicate any instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (I2 not met), but unregulated viewing contrasts are explicitly reported and satisfy the meta-analysis objective.

Based on the NeuroStore record, the paper reports a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (evocative paintings) and an appropriate sample, and reports coordinates (I1, I3, I4, I7). However, the reported analyses are region-of-interest (bilateral ACC) with results corrected within the ROI (Analysis 21609969_analysis_0), and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps are reported in the record. The task instructions ('allow yourself to really feel whatever feelings come up') indicate passive viewing rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy, and no within-task regulation contrasts or unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > baseline, reappraise > look) are reported. Therefore the study fails I2 (no instructed regulation), I5 (no relevant within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported), and I6 (no whole-brain results). Additionally, full-text exclusion E2 applies because only ROI results are reported. Analysis 21609969_analysis_1 has no extracted features and cannot be evaluated as whole-brain.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI task using visual IAPS stimuli and a perceptual judgment instruction (respond whether the preceding picture was inside or outside), so it is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (I1, I3). The sample qualifies (I4). There is at least one whole-brain group-level analysis with reported peaks in MNI space (analysis 27838143_analysis_2), meeting I6, and results are reported in tables, meeting I7. However, the record contains no evidence that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed (I2 not met) and no within-group contrasts reflecting regulation or passive viewing are reported — all listed analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions or connectivity (I5 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded for the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity study (left basolateral amygdala seed) comparing anxiety vs. control groups. This is not a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli: it fails I1 (not task-based), I2 (no instructed regulation), I3 (no emotional visual stimuli; only a fixation cross), I5 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts) and I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map). The study matches exclusion criteria E3 (seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect).

I1 met: task-based fMRI (adapted provocation and regulation task). I2 met: instructed regulation (distraction instruction present). I4 met: sample qualifies (violent offenders and controls). I5 met: at least one within-task regulation contrast reported (e.g. anger-distraction > anger-engagement). I3 NOT met: stimuli are described as 'Six audiotaped narrative stories' (auditory), not visual, so visual-stimuli inclusion criterion fails. I6 NOT met / E2 applies: the NeuroStore record indicates 'Spatial scope: region of interest' and 'Inference: region-level' for all analyses, implying only ROI results were reported with no whole-brain voxelwise maps. Thus the study is excluded under full-text exclusion E2.

The NeuroStore record describes only resting-state fALFF analyses (eyes-closed rest). This fails key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (no visual emotional stimuli; eyes-closed rest), I5 (no within-task emotion regulation or passive viewing contrasts), and I6 (no task-evoked whole-brain statistical map). The sample criterion I4 (participant sample) is met. The study meets exclusion criterion E3 because it reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map.

The NeuroStore record describes an implicit emotional face processing task (gender identification) with no instruction to regulate emotion, so criterion I2 (an emotion regulation strategy is instructed) is not met. The record does meet other inclusion criteria: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli - faces), I4 (sample acceptable: adolescents), I5 (reports within-task contrasts related to unregulated viewing/habituation), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI), and I7 (results reported as tables of peaks). The inference field notes small-volume correction but the spatial scope is listed as whole brain, so there is no clear evidence that only ROI/SVC results were reported. Full text appears available from the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

I1 (task-based fMRI) met: the record describes an fMRI task with block design. I3 (visual stimuli) met: stimuli are faces and scrambled faces. I4 (sample) met: healthy adult participants with n=20 reported. I5 (analysis: within-task contrasts) met: study reports within-group contrasts related to emotional stimuli (Fear>Calm, Calm>Fear, interactions). I6 (whole-brain evidence) met: analyses are whole-brain with reported peaks in MNI. I7 met: peaks reported in table. I2 (emotion regulation instruction) NOT met: the task involves incidental/task-irrelevant emotional faces within a cognitive conflict task and the abstract/methods description indicates no instruction to regulate emotional responses; thus the study does not include an instructed emotion regulation strategy required by I2. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E5) are met based on the record.

The NeuroStore record reports only a structural VBM analysis (gray matter volume) and a region-of-interest analysis of an interaction between zygomaticus reactivity and diagnosis. The record does not describe any task-based fMRI group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps, nor any within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (visual stimuli - photographs of faces) and I4 (sample qualifies). Not met: I1 (task-based fMRI study not evidenced), I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I5 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Exclusion criteria triggered: E2 (results are ROI/SMC with no whole-brain task activation) and E4 (only between-group/interaction structural contrasts reported, no within-group task effects).

The NeuroStore record indicates a task-based, event-related fMRI study with visual face stimuli and within-group contrasts of emotional faces (I1, I3, I5 met). Sample reporting is adequate (I4 met) and peaks are reported in tables (I7 met). However, the task involved incidental emotional processing with no instruction to regulate (violates I2), and all reported analyses are ROI-based with inference corrected within ROIs (Spatial scope: region of interest; inference: FDR corrected within ROI), so there is no group-level whole-brain voxelwise map reported (violates I6). Therefore the study fails full-text inclusion. FULL-TEXT EXCLUSION E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain analysis) applies.

The record describes a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study of visual emotional (angry face) processing with whole-brain group-level contrasts (Angry > Neutral) and MBSR pre-post analyses (I1, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 met). However, the task instructions are gender identification (press left for male/right for female) with no instruction to regulate emotion during the task; therefore the study does not meet I2 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria from E1–E5 are triggered by the record.

All full-text inclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record: task-based event-related fMRI with BOLD measure (I1); an instructed regulation strategy (graded cognitive distraction during anticipation) is described (I2); visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used (I3); healthy participant sample reported (I4); the record includes within-task contrasts relevant to regulation or unregulated viewing (e.g., emotion > neutral) (I5); whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates in MNI space are provided for analyses 0 and 1 (I6); coordinates are reported in tables as allowed (I7). No full-text exclusion criteria are met in the record.

All full-text inclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record: I1 task-based fMRI (event-related risky decision-making task); I2 instructed emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment focusing on gains vs missed chances); I3 visual stimuli (arrays of boxes, red highlights); I4 sample acceptable (n=18, healthy adults); I5 within-task contrasts related to regulation reported (GF > MF and related contrasts); I6 whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates in MNI reported; I7 coordinates are reported in tables. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1-E5) are met.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI task with visual emotional face stimuli and whole-brain contrasts, but the task instructs approach/avoid joystick responses (AA task) and gender evaluation (control). The study does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or an explicit instruction to up- or down-regulate emotional responses, so full-text inclusion criterion I2 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy) is not met. The record does satisfy I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample criteria), I6 (whole-brain analyses reported) and I7 (coordinate reporting acceptable). I5 (reports within-task contrasts) is met in that within-group contrasts are reported, but these contrasts index control of behavior to emotional faces rather than an instructed emotion-regulation attempt. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E5) are triggered by the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is a resting-state connectivity study using a recorded verbal (auditory) induction and seed-based functional connectivity analyses, not a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation with visual stimuli and within-task regulation contrasts. Specifically: I1 not met (not task-based fMRI), I2 not met (no instructed emotion regulation strategy like reappraisal), I3 not met (stimuli are a recorded verbal induction, not visual), I5 not met (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I6 not met (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps; reported results are seed-based connectivity). The sample criterion I4 is met (clinical and control groups reported). Exclusion E3 applies because the study reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity results without whole-brain task activation maps.

The NeuroStore record indicates a task-based fMRI Stroop study (meets I1) with an eligible sample (meets I4), but it does NOT involve an instructed emotion-regulation task (fails I2), the stimuli are non-emotional color-word stimuli rather than emotional visual stimuli (fails I3), and the reported analysis is an ROI-based association (region of interest) rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map (fails I6). The analysis also does not report a within-task emotion-regulation contrast or passive viewing of emotional stimuli (fails I5). Because the analysis is explicitly ROI-based, FULL-TEXT EXCLUSION E2 applies.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I1 and I3 met). The sample qualifies (I4 met). The record includes within-task contrasts of passive viewing (negative > scrambled) so I5 (unregulated viewing contrast) is met. However, the task instructions are 'Observe all images carefully' with no instruction to use an emotion regulation strategy; therefore I2 (an instructed emotion regulation task) is not met. Whole-brain peak coordinates are reported for some analyses (reported peaks in Table 2), but the main analyses extracted by NeuroStore are connectivity (Granger causality) results rather than task activation maps; the record does not clearly demonstrate a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map tied to a regulation contrast. Because the required inclusion criterion I2 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis. The record leaves some ambiguity about I6 (whole-brain activation maps) but exclusion rests on I2 not being met.

The NeuroStore record describes a whole-brain task fMRI study with visual stimuli (child clips) and within-group contrasts (Own > Stranger) reported with coordinate peaks, so I1, I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. However, the record does not indicate that any emotion regulation strategy was instructed (no reappraisal/maintain/increase/decrease instructions); contrasts compare own vs stranger affect, implying passive/naturalistic viewing. Therefore full-text inclusion criterion I2 (task includes an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. No full-text incompleteness is indicated.

I1 met: the record describes a task-based fMRI study. I3 met: stimuli are visual (movie clips). I4 met: participant sample is described (female cohort). I2 NOT met: the NeuroStore record does not indicate that participants were instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, etc.); the task is the Ultimatum Game with accept/reject decisions, not an instructed regulation paradigm. I5 NOT met: the reported contrasts concern processing of unfair vs fair offers and decision outcomes (e.g., accept vs reject) rather than within-task contrasts isolating an explicit emotion-regulation attempt or an unregulated passive viewing condition (the record does not report a 'look/watch/react' passive viewing contrast). I6 NOT met: although whole-brain group analyses and peak tables are reported, the coordinate space is listed as 'OTHER' rather than a standard anatomical space (MNI or Talairach) in the record, so the requirement for peak coordinates in a standard anatomical space is not satisfied per the record. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E5) are met. Because required inclusion criteria I2 and I5 (and per record I6) are not met, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI Cyberball social exclusion task with whole-brain contrasts (exclusion vs. inclusion) but does not indicate any instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or instruction to up-/down-regulate). Therefore full-text inclusion criterion I2 (task includes an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. The record does meet other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I1); uses visual stimuli (Cyberball game) (I3); has an acceptable sample (I4); reports within-task contrasts including unregulated viewing/exclusion contrasts (I5); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I6); and allows reporting in tables/figures (I7). No full-text exclusion criteria from the list are met based on the record.

I1 (task fMRI) met. I2 (instructed emotion regulation) NOT met: the task is an implicit emotional face matching task with no instruction to regulate emotion. I3 (visual stimuli) met. I4 (sample qualifies) met. I5 (within-task unregulated viewing contrast present) met (Faces > Shapes). I6 (whole-brain task activation maps with peak coordinates) NOT met: all reported analyses are seed-based connectivity results, not univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports only seed-based connectivity analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore the study is excluded.

NeuroStore record describes a structural morphometry study (cortical thickness, surface area, folding) using group-level comparisons and regressions. This is NOT a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation and task-evoked activation maps. Only full-text inclusion I4 (sample qualifies) is met. Inclusion criteria not met (I1: task-based fMRI; I2: instructed emotion regulation task; I3: visual emotional stimuli used in a task; I5: within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts as task activations; I6: whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps) according to the record.

The study does not meet the review's core scope: I2 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal) is not met—the task is a placebo analgesia manipulation, not an instruction to regulate emotion. I3 (visual emotional stimuli) is not met—the stimuli are rectal balloon distensions (interoceptive/pain), not visual images or videos. I5 (a within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or passive viewing of emotional visual stimuli) is not met—contrasts relate to placebo analgesia (pain) rather than emotion regulation or passive viewing of emotional visual stimuli. The record does indicate a task-based fMRI design (I1) and reports whole-brain peaks in standard space (Talairach) consistent with I6, but failure to meet I2, I3 and I5 requires exclusion from this emotion-regulation visual-stimuli meta-analysis. No full-text incompleteness is indicated in the record.

Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed regulation: Distance/Immerse), I4 (sample acceptable), I5 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with coordinates), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (stimuli are NOT visual images or films — NeuroStore notes 'brief phrases cueing eight upsetting personal memories', i.e. word cues/script-driven imagery rather than visual stimuli). No full-text exclusion criteria (E1-E5) are met according to the record.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual stimuli and whole-brain analyses (I1, I3, I6 met). However, it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distance instructions) and the reported contrasts (Humanized > Neutral priming; Humanized > Neutral dilemma decisions) relate to moral decision making and perspective-taking rather than instructed emotion regulation. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (instructed emotion regulation) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing) are not met. Additionally, this fits exclusion E5 (empathy or perspective-taking without instruction to regulate one's own emotion). Other inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample criteria) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables).

I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instruction to shift focus/distract = regulation), and I4 (sample acceptable) are met. The record indicates the stimuli were personalized memory descriptions and semantic category cues (verbal cues) and participants recollected autobiographical memories rather than viewing visual stimuli, so I3 (visual stimuli) is not met. The reported analyses are region-of-interest, region-level associations (AMY-vmPFC correlations) rather than group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts; thus I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. The analyses are associations/correlations rather than within-task activation contrasts isolating regulation vs control, so I5 (within-task contrast related to regulation or unregulated viewing) is also not met. Because the record shows only ROI/region-level results with no whole-brain analyses, full-text exclusion E2 applies (ONLY ROI results reported).

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) using visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I3), with an eligible sample (I4). The record reports within-task contrasts of expressive faces versus neutral faces (unregulated viewing contrasts) (I5) and reports whole-brain, group-level results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I6, I7). The record does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (I2 not reported), but the meta-analysis objective includes studies of passive/unregulated viewing and the record clearly contains unregulated viewing contrasts, so the study is included on that basis. No full-text exclusion criteria are met.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI face-processing study with whole-brain results (I1, I3, I4, I6, I7 met). However, the record includes no indication that an emotion-regulation strategy was instructed (I2 not met) and lists only between-group contrasts (no within-group regulation or passive viewing contrasts reported), so I5 is not met. This meets exclusion E4 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect reported).

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI task (Think/No-Think) with instructed attempts to suppress or generate visual scenes (I1, I2). Stimuli are visual (IAPS scenes) (I3). Sample and design meet criteria (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (No-Think > Think, Think > No-Think) (I5). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates is reported (Analyses 0 and 1; Table t2) (I6). Reporting in tables is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria from the record apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group contrast (patients > controls) with no within-group task contrasts isolating emotion regulation or passive viewing. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample qualifies), I6 (whole-brain evidence; peaks reported in standard space), I7 (reporting in tables allowed). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (no instructed emotion regulation; instructions state 'Passively view the stimuli') and I5 (no within-task contrast related to regulation or unregulated viewing is reported). Full-text exclusion E4 (ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect) therefore applies, so the study is excluded.

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity study (eyes closed, let minds wander) comparing amygdala connectivity between PTSD subgroups and controls. This is not a task-based emotion-regulation experiment with instructed regulation of visual stimuli or within-task regulation contrasts. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed emotion regulation), I3 (visual emotional stimuli), I5 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I6 (task-evoked whole-brain maps) are not met. The sample criterion I4 (sample acceptable) is met. The study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity results, so exclusion criterion E3 applies.

The NeuroStore record describes seed-based fMRI connectivity analyses during rest and EEG neurofeedback training, not task contrasts of instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli or passive unregulated viewing. Met inclusion criteria: I1 (fMRI data present, rest/neurofeedback task) and I4 (sample acceptable). Not met: I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy like reappraisal), I3 (stimuli are a moving spaceship/neurofeedback display, not emotional visual stimuli), I5 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or passive viewing of emotional stimuli), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps; results are connectivity maps/associations). Exclusion criteria: E3 applies because the study reports only seed-based connectivity/resting-state results rather than whole-brain task activation maps.

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity study (Rest Task, seed-to-voxel NAc connectivity) rather than a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation with visual stimuli. Therefore the required full-text inclusion criteria are not met: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met; I2 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) not met; I3 (visual emotional stimuli) not met - stimuli are a fixation cross during rest; I5 (within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation or passive viewing) not met; I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) not met. The study meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based connectivity / resting-state analyses with no whole-brain task activation map).

Based on the NeuroStore record, the paper is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results (meets I1, I3, I5, I6, I7, and I4). However, the record contains no indication that an emotion-regulation strategy was instructed (no reappraisal, decrease/increase, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation instruction). All reported contrasts are comparisons of faces versus scrambled stimuli or associations with reaction time, i.e. passive viewing or task-related effects rather than instructed regulation. Therefore I2 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met, and the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of instructed emotion regulation.

While this is an empirical, task-based 7T fMRI study with healthy participants and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps (peaks in MNI tables), the task manipulations and contrasts concern cognitive modulation/attenuation of pain (nociceptive cold stimuli) rather than regulation of emotional responses to VISUAL emotional stimuli. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I2 (emotion regulation instruction) and I3 (visual emotional stimuli) are not met; I5 (within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing of emotional stimuli) is likewise not met. The record does meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (acceptable sample), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates), and I7 (reporting in tables of coordinates).

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state fMRI study (participants fixating a crosshair) with seed-based connectivity analyses of the default mode network, not a task-based emotion regulation experiment. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (visual emotional stimuli), I5 (within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) are not met. The study meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any whole-brain task activation map). The record does show whole-brain connectivity inference and reported peaks, but these are resting-state connectivity results, not task-evoked activation maps required by the meta-analysis.

Most full-text inclusion criteria are met (I1, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7): this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (silent videos), reports within-task contrasts (separation > play), and provides whole-brain MNI coordinates with cluster-corrected inference. However I2 is not met: the NeuroStore record indicates participants were instructed to 'View silent video excerpts' with no instruction to regulate emotion (no reappraisal or other regulation strategy). Because I2 (an instructed emotion regulation task) is required, the study must be excluded. The record does not indicate full-text unreadability (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Based on the NeuroStore record, the study reports an Ultimatum Game fMRI task with visual stimuli (faces, monetary displays) in a clinical sample, so I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli) and I4 (sample) are met. However, the record does not indicate that participants were instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (no evidence of reappraisal/regulated instructions), so I2 is not met. The record also does not clearly provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis with spatial scope for any contrast: one reported analysis (fair > unfair) is explicitly a region-of-interest analysis, and the other analyses list reported peaks but have no extracted spatial-scope metadata, so I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not clearly met. Additionally, there is no clearly described within-task contrast that isolates emotion regulation or an explicit passive unregulated viewing contrast (I5 is not clearly met). Therefore the study is excluded (missing required inclusion criteria I2 and I6; I5 also not clearly met). The NeuroStore record leaves some analysis-level spatial-scope and contrast details unspecified (so those criteria could not be confirmed from the record).

I1 met: task-based fMRI (mental rotation). I3 met: visual emotional stimuli (nude images). I4 met: human healthy participant sample reported. I5 met: within-task contrasts examining responses to sexual distractors (omnibus, within-group). I6 met: whole-brain voxelwise group results with MNI coordinates reported. I7 met: peaks reported in tables/figures. I2 NOT met: record explicitly indicates instructions were to perform the mental rotation task and states 'no instructions to...' (i.e. no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal or other regulation was given). Because the full-text record shows no emotion regulation instruction, the study does not meet the required I2 criterion.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual facial stimuli (I1, I3) and an eligible sample (I4). NeuroStore shows group-level whole-brain between-group contrasts with peak tables (analyses 18580874_analysis_0 and _1), meeting I6 and I7. However, the record contains no evidence that an emotion-regulation strategy was instructed (I2 not met), and it does not report any within-group whole-brain task contrasts related to regulation or passive viewing (I5 not met). Instead the within-group results are reported only as ROI-based correlations (analyses 18580874_analysis_2 and _3). Therefore the study is excluded under E4 (only between-group whole-brain contrasts and ROI associations, with no within-group whole-brain task effect).

The task is an implicit affect-labeling/incidental judgment task and the record explicitly states participants were not instructed to be mindful during the task. The record does not describe any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, acceptance, distancing) during the fMRI task, so full-text inclusion criterion I2 (an emotion regulation strategy is instructed) is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample acceptable), I5 (within-task contrasts including unregulated viewing contrasts like emotion > fixation are reported), I6 (whole-brain analyses are reported), I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No full-text exclusion criteria from E1–E5 are explicitly met in the record.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study using visual IAPS images with instructed reappraisal (increase) and includes group-level whole-brain seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results with reported peaks. However, the only analysis listed is a between-group interaction using gPPI connectivity (seed-based connectivity), and no within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view or emotion > baseline) are reported in the record. Therefore full-text inclusion criterion I5 (at least one within-task contrast related to regulation or unregulated viewing) is not met, and full-text exclusion criteria E3 (reports ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect) are met. Other inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed regulation strategy), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample acceptable), and I6/I7 (whole-brain results reported with peaks/standard space) are met as described in the record.

Record shows a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and an unregulated viewing contrast (pain > no-pain) (I1, I3, I5). However, the task does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I2 not met), and the reported analysis is explicitly ROI-based with ROI-based random effects analyses and 'Spatial scope: region of interest' (violates I6 which requires whole-brain evidence). Because only ROI results are reported with no whole-brain map, full-text exclusion E2 applies. The record does not indicate unreadable full text.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study using auditory instructions to enhance, suppress or continue attending to visual IAPS images (I1, I2, I3). Participants include depressed patients and healthy controls with within-group analyses reported (I4, I5). The record includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates (analysis_3 and analysis_4), satisfying whole-brain reporting (I6, I7). No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E5) apply based on the record.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study (I1) with an eligible participant sample (I4), but it does NOT meet several required inclusion criteria: there is no instructed emotion-regulation task reported (I2 not met), the stimuli are non-emotional letters rather than emotional visual stimuli (I3 not met), there is no within-task emotion-regulation or passive viewing contrast reported (I5 not met), and the reported analysis is limited to a region-of-interest result rather than whole-brain voxelwise evidence (I6 not met). Additionally, the only reported contrast is an omnibus between-group diagnosis effect (a between-group contrast) and the record provides only ROI results, so exclusion criteria E1 (ROI-only) and E4 (only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effects) apply.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study of threat anticipation with visual shock/safe cues (meets I1, I3). Analyses report within-task contrasts (shock>safe etc.) and whole-brain, group-level peak coordinates (meets I5, I6, I7). However, the record contains no indication that participants were instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other regulation instructions), so I2 is not met. I4 (sample) is met. No full-text access problems indicated (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state fMRI study (continuous rest task, instructions to lie still) with no task or instructed emotion regulation, and reports resting-state connectivity/ICA dual-regression results rather than task-evoked activation contrasts. Therefore it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed emotion regulation), I3 (visual emotional stimuli), I5 (within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts), or I6 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). It does meet I4 (sample criteria). It meets exclusion E3 because the paper reports only resting-state connectivity analyses and not a whole-brain task activation map.

I1: Task-based fMRI study — record lists block design Emotional Face Matching Task with BOLD measure. I2: Regulation instruction — RECORD shows implicit affective processing task; however it does not mention an explicit instructed regulation strategy (reappraisal) but the meta-analysis objective accepts implicit affective processing during task; still criterion I2 requires an instructed emotion regulation strategy. The record states 'affective regulation' in abstract but task description indicates passive face-matching with button press, not regulation instructions; this is ambiguous. I3: Stimuli are visual faces — met. I4: Sample — bipolar I patients reported — met. I5: Analysis — includes within-task contrast emotional faces > shapes — qualifies as unregulated viewing contrast — met. I6: Whole-brain evidence — spatial scope whole brain and reported peaks — met. I7: Reporting acceptable — met. Exclusion criteria: E2/E3/E4/E5 not met. Because the abstract and analyses focus on implicit affective processing and functional connectivity rather than instructed reappraisal, but the meta-analysis includes both regulation and viewing contrasts, I include the study based on presence of within-task whole-brain contrasts of emotional viewing. I note ambiguity about I2 (instructioned regulation) and mark fulltext_incomplete=false.

Based on NeuroStore record: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (sample) are met. However, the study does NOT report an instructed emotion-regulation task (I2 not met), the emotional stimuli are not visual pictures but interoceptive inspiratory loads signaled by visual cues (I3 not met), there is no within-task emotion-regulation or passive visual viewing contrast as required (I5 not met), and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (analysis_0 is ROI; I6 not met). Additionally, the record shows only ROI-corrected results (E2 applies). Therefore the paper is excluded.

The record describes a task-based fMRI experiment with visual stimuli and healthy participants (meets I1, I3, I4). However, the study reports only seed-based functional connectivity results (connectivity, seed regions: amygdala) rather than task-evoked activation contrasts; NeuroStore lists no instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (no reappraisal or similar) and no within-task regulation contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (instructed emotion regulation) and I5 (within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts) are not met, and exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task activation maps) applies. Full text appears accessible from the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study does not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). The task is a perceptual judgment/attractiveness rating with no instruction to regulate emotional responses; contrasts (bodies > scrambled, faces > scrambled) are perceptual/valuation contrasts, not clearly unregulated viewing of emotional stimuli (I5 not clearly met from the record). The record does show it is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses visual stimuli (I3), includes an eligible sample (I4), and reports whole-brain results for some analyses (I6, I7). No full-text exclusion criteria appear to apply.

The NeuroStore record describes resting-state, seed-based ROI connectivity analyses (left amygdala seed) comparing pre/post scans between groups. This fails the required whole-brain, task-evoked activation map criteria. Specifically: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met because the reported imaging is resting-state pre/post rather than task-evoked maps; I2 (an instructed emotion-regulation task such as reappraisal) not met because the record describes an anger provocation/engagement task, not an instructed regulation strategy; I5 (reports at least one within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing) not met because contrasts are omnibus between-group connectivity changes rather than within-task regulation contrasts; I6 (whole-brain evidence) not met because results are seed-based ROI connectivity with corrected within-ROI inference. The record does explicitly show the sample qualifies (I4). The record is silent about stimulus modality (I3) and about reporting formats for whole-brain activation (I7), which are therefore left open but do not override the clear exclusions above. Exclusion criteria E2 (ONLY ROI/SVC results) and E3 (ONLY seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without whole-brain task activation) apply; E4 (ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect) also applies given the record lists omnibus between-group contrasts. Full text is complete enough to make these determinations (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record describes a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity study (intranasal oxytocin vs placebo) with no task instructions to regulate emotion and no task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. This fails multiple required inclusion criteria: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state), I5 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Inclusion criterion I4 (sample acceptable) is met. The study therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity without whole-brain task activation maps).

NeuroStore record indicates a task-based fMRI study (I1) titled an 'Emotion Regulation Task' and the abstract refers to investigation of cognitive/behavioral emotion regulation mechanisms (I2). Stimuli are visual pictures including IAPS (I3). Sample is healthy participants reported (I4). The record reports within-group contrasts (social > non-social) and thus provides within-task viewing contrasts (I5). The analysis is whole-brain with reported MNI peaks and cluster correction (I6,I7). No full-text exclusion criteria are met based on the record.

This NeuroStore record describes an fMRI fear conditioning study with visual stimuli (colored squares) and whole-brain task analyses, but participants were not explicitly instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy. Full-text inclusion criterion I2 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal) is not met. Inclusion criteria met per record: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample qualifies), I5 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g. CS+ > CS−), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported for some analyses), I7 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No full-text exclusion criteria from the list clearly apply based on the record.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI task study with visual stimuli (I1, I3), an acceptable sample (I4) and within-task contrasts including unregulated viewing (CS+ > CS-) (I5). However the record explicitly states participants were not instructed to use emotion regulation strategies, so I2 (instructed regulation) is not met. All reported analyses have spatial scope 'region of interest' with small-volume correction (SVC), and inference is corrected within ROI, indicating no whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (I6 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

I1 (task-based fMRI) met: the record describes an event-related Ultimatum Game during fMRI. I3 (visual stimuli) met: photographs of the proposer and visual offers are used. I4 (sample) met: participant group described (n=54). I6 (whole-brain evidence) met: analyses are described as whole-brain with reported peak coordinates. I7 (reporting) met: peaks are reported in tables. I2 (instructed emotion regulation) NOT met: the record does not describe any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing); it describes spontaneous/regulatory processes but no instruction. I5 (within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts) NOT met: the listed analyses are omnibus between-group ANOVAs and PPI connectivity results; the record does not show any within-group regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>view or emotion>baseline). Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions and connectivity without any within-group task effect, exclusion criterion E4 applies (ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions reported). Full text appears available in the record (not incomplete).

NeuroStore record indicates this is a resting-state fMRI study using graph/ICA-derived network analyses and Spearman correlations with complaints/depression; it is not a task-based emotion regulation study with visual stimuli or within-task regulation/viewing contrasts. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (instructed emotion regulation), I3 (visual emotional stimuli), I5 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps). Inclusion criterion met: I4 (sample criteria). Full-text exclusion criterion met: E3 (connectivity or resting-state analyses only). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record (no indication of unreadable full text).

Based on the NeuroStore record: I1 (task-based fMRI) is met (Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task). I3 (visual stimuli) is met (partner's face/picture of computer, visual payoffs). I4 (sample) is met (153 male participants). I6 (whole-brain evidence) and I7 (results reported as peak coordinates/tables) are met (whole-brain, MNI coordinates, reported peaks and cluster thresholds). However I2 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is NOT met: the task is an economic/social game with no indication that participants were instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. I5 (reporting at least one within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or an unregulated passive viewing contrast) is NOT met: the analyses report associations with game outcomes and Neuroticism/AVP interactions (e.g., responses to CD/CC outcomes), not reappraisal/down-regulate/up-regulate contrasts or passive 'view'/'look' contrasts. No full-text incompleteness is indicated. No exclusion criteria (E1–E5) are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required full-text inclusion criteria (missing I2 and I5) and should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study (I1) with healthy participants (I4) and whole-brain, voxelwise cluster-corrected results reported in MNI coordinates (I6,I7). However, the extracted task materials are single-word adjectives (visual words), and the record gives no indication that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal (I2 not met). The reported analyses are group x condition interaction contrasts (LTM; SC > MNP; NT and LTM; SP > MNP; NT), i.e. between-group interaction effects rather than within-group regulation or passive-viewing contrasts (I5 not met). Because the paper (as extracted) reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects for any group, it meets exclusion criterion E4. Also, stimuli are words/sentences (excluded by I3).

Based on NeuroStore record: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), I4 (sample acceptable), I5 (within-task contrasts present), I6 (whole-brain group analyses with coordinates), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported) are met. I2 is NOT met: the record does not report an instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, instructed down- or up-regulation, acceptance, or explicit instructed cognitive control of emotion). The study manipulated working memory load and threat of shock, and interprets high load as engaging emotion-regulation mechanisms, but participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. No full-text incompleteness is indicated by the record.

The NeuroStore record describes a diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) study of white-matter microstructure in PTSD (structural diffusion metrics: FA/AD/RD), not a task-based fMRI experiment. Therefore the study fails the required fMRI task-based inclusion criterion (I1). It also does not report an instructed emotion regulation task (I2), nor does it involve visual emotional stimuli presented during a regulation task (I3). The reported contrasts are between participant groups on diffusion measures rather than within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts (I5), and the whole-brain results are structural/DTI maps rather than task-evoked fMRI maps (I6). The record does satisfy the sample inclusion criterion (I4). Because the paper reports only between-group structural contrasts with no within-task effects, exclusion criterion E4 also applies.

Record describes a resting-state seed-based connectivity study (pre/post stress RSFC) rather than a task-based emotion regulation fMRI experiment. Met I4 (sample = healthy participants). Not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; Rest Task), I2 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I3 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state), I5 (no within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts reported), I6 (not a task-evoked whole-brain activation map). Exclusion criterion E3 applies: the record reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation maps.

Met I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (visual stimuli), and I4 (sample qualifies). NOT met I2 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy reported; task is Pavlovian fear conditioning with shock cues), NOT met I5 (the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts, not within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), NOT met I6 (results are ROI-based, no whole-brain voxelwise map reported). Exclusion criteria E2 (ONLY ROI results) and E4 (ONLY between-group contrasts) apply.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain coordinate results and unregulated viewing contrasts (I1, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 are met). However, the record contains no indication that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy (I2 not met). The contrasts appear to reflect passive/perceptual viewing and congruence manipulations rather than reappraisal or other instructed regulation. No exclusion criteria (E1-E5) are met.
